assessment: The proposal is largely sound: all five scientific branches correspond to literal source call sites; endpoint recovery for the two never-observed outputs (full-backbone group series, open↔closed scalar) is a documented faithful rerun of unchanged source calls, permitted by endpoint_recovery policy; the DCD AKMA time-label caveat is verified against MDAnalysis 2.9.0 DCD.py; the solver-facing brief stands alone and withholds answers; and the answer-bearing test fixture MDAnalysisTests/analysis/test_rms.py (4.68953 / 0.91544906) is correctly excluded with content identity and a runtime-verified no-effect claim. However, a source check of the pinned implementation reveals one blocking scientific mis-specification. MDAnalysis 2.9.0 analysis/rms.py RMSD._prepare (sdist lines 670–690) propagates weights='mass' to groupselections when weights_groupselections keeps its default False: iterable('mass') is False for strings (lib/util.py, lines 1102–1106), so the code assigns self.weights_groupselections = [self.weights] * len(self.groupselections) and converts each entry to the group atoms' masses; the class docstring confirms ('mass' will use masses as weights for both select and groupselections; False 'will apply imposed weights to groupselections from weights option if weights is either \"mass\" or None'). Consequently the CORE/LID/NMP columns of the recorded reference rmsd_mass_weighted.csv are mass-weighted, contradicting the notebook narrative ('these remain unweighted below', stale relative to 2.9.0) that the brief inherited for output 4(d): the brief demands unweighted group RMSDs, so a solver who follows the brief exactly would produce scientifically different values (backbone N/CA/C/O masses are not uniform) and be graded wrong, or grading would use an answer key inconsistent with its own stated definition. This is a concrete, correctable defect that must be fixed by the writer before assets freeze, together with the corresponding failure-probe gap. All other definitions (fit selections, frame-0 reference, shared single fit, center-of-geometry centering, weight vectors for outputs 1, 2, 3 and 5) were verified against the source and the recorded artifacts; uncalibrated tolerances are correctly deferred to executable validation and do not block.

findings.problem: Output 4 (mass-weighted series, (d)) specifies the CORE/LID/NMP backbone-subset RMSDs as unweighted. This claim is lifted from the source notebook narrative, but under the pinned reference implementation (MDAnalysis 2.9.0) it is false: MDAnalysis/analysis/rms.py RMSD._prepare propagates weights='mass' to groupselections whenever weights_groupselections keeps its default False (iterable('mass') is False for strings, so the code assigns [self.weights] * len(groupselections), subsequently converted to each group's per-atom masses), and the class docstring documents this ('mass' will use masses as weights for both select and groupselections). The recorded reference rmsd_mass_weighted.csv was generated by exactly this code path on the same inputs, so its CORE/LID/NMP columns are mass-weighted values. Backbones contain N/CA/C/O atoms of differing masses, so the unweighted and mass-weighted group RMSDs differ measurably; a solver following the brief as written would compute scientifically different results that fail grading, or grading would use an answer key inconsistent with its own stated definition.
